title: City of Bremerton v. Widell
questions: Whether a defendant charged with criminal trespass for entering a housing authority complex in violation of an exclusion order may challenge the validity of that order, and if so, whether the orders in this case, and the housing authority policy underlying them are valid under the common law of property, the first amendment to the federal constitution and the Washington and federal due process clauses.

title: State of Washington v. McNeal
questions: Whether an irreconcilable inconsistency between a general verdict on a vehicular assault charge and a special verdict on a separate vehicular homicide charge requires vacation of either conviction under RCW 4.44.440, which provides that special verdicts shall control inconsistent general verdicts.

title: Isla Verde International v. State of Washington
questions: Whether a condition requiring a subdivision developer to set aside 30 percent of the land as open space constituted a "dedication" of land subject to constitutional takings analysis under Dolan v. City of Tigard, 512 U.S. 374, 114 S. Ct. 2309, 129 L. Ed. 2d 304 (1994).

title: State of Washington v. Bryant
questions: Whether a derivative use immunity agreement between the defendant and the King County Prosecuting Attorney, covering "any prosecution," precludes a prosecution in Snohomish County using evidence derived from the defendant's statements to King County authorities.

title: Grant County Fire Protection District No. 5 v. City of Moses Lake
questions: Whether the property-owner-petition method of annexing territory by a city under RCW 35.13.125-160 or RCW 35A.14.120-150 is unconstitutional under the equal protection clause of the United States constitution or Article I Sections 12 or 19 of the Washington State Constitution.

title: Grant County Fire Protection District No. 5 v. City of Moses Lake
questions: Whether the property-owner-petition method of annexing territory by a city under RCW 35.13.125-160 or RCW 35A.14.120-150 is unconstitutional under the equal protection clause of the United States constitution or Article I Sections 12 or 19 of the Washington State Constitution.

title: In re Petersen
questions: In a sexually violent predator proceeding, which party has the burden of proof and by what standard at an annual review probable cause hearing.

title: Jones v. Allstate Insurance
questions: Whether an insurance company engaged in the negligent or unauthorized practice of law by virtue of the manner in which it dealt with and settled a third party's claim against one of its insureds.

title: Sackett v. Santilli
questions: Whether CR 38 violates WASH. CONST. art I sec. 21 by providing a judicially created means to waive the right to a jury trial in a civil litigation

title: State of Washington v. Sanchez
questions: Whether a state agent other than the prosecutor is bound by a prosecutor's promise, in a plea bargain, to recommend a particular sentence.

title: State of Washington v. Harris
questions: Whether a state agent other than the prosecutor is bound by a prosecutor's promise, in a plea bargain, to recommend a particular sentence.

title: Rios v. Department of Labor & Industries
questions: Whether the Court of Appeals properly held that L&I is required by the Washington Industrial Safety and Health Act to adopt mandatory cholinesterase monitoring for agricultural workers exposed to pesticides.

title: Overton v. Consolidated Insurance
questions: Whether an insured's alleged knowledge of PCB contamination prior to purchase of a comprehensive general liability policy precludes coverage; and whether the insurer acted in bad faith when it refused to defend a lawsuit.

title: Asarco, Inc. v. Department of Ecology
questions: Whether recent developments in the jurisprudence of substantive due process and takings has rendered the Model Toxics Control Act unconstitutional when applied to certain aging hazardous waste sites.

title: Robel v. Roundup Corp.
questions: Did the Court of Appeals correctly reverse a bench-trial judgment for petitioner on her claims for disability harassment, retaliation for filing a workers' compensation claim, negligent infliction of emotional distress, outrage, and defamation?

title: State of Washington v. Norman
questions: Defendants maintain that because the state constitution defines Washington's northern boundary in relevant part as the 49th parallel, the State does not have jurisdiction to prosecute them for crimes committed south of the international border between the United States and Canada, but north of the 49th parallel as currently located.

title: In re Marriage of Litowitz
questions: Whether the Court of Appeals was correct when it awarded Petitioner, David J. Litowitz, two frozen embryos in a dissolution action and whether Petitioner's motion to submit additional evidence should be granted.

title: Benchmark Land Co. v. City of Battle Ground
questions: Whether a city's condition for subdivision approval, requiring a developer to make improvements to a street bordering its proposed development, triggers the takings analysis of Dolan v. City of Tigard, 512 U.S. 374, 114 S. Ct. 2309, 129 L. Ed. 2d 304 (1994).

title: International Ass'n of Firefighters, Local 1789 v. Spokane Airports
questions: Whether an association has standing to bring suit on behalf of its members where it seeks monetary damages only. Whether the association had a contractual obligation to exhaust arbitration before bringing suit. Whether, after firefighters opted out of the social security system, their employer was obligated to pay into the firefighters' pension plan amounts equal to the matching social security contributions it had previously paid.

title: State of Washington v. Darden
questions: Whether the trial court's exclusion of evidence of a police officer's precise surveillance location violated the defendant's right to confrontation.

title: ATU Legislative v. State of Washington
Howe v. Douglas County
questions: Whether a county may enforce a waiver, imposed as a condition of plat approval, by which a developer waived any damage claims of its successors-in-interest based on the construction and maintenance of storm drainage facilities that the developer transferred to the county.

title: International Ass'n of Fire Fighters, Local 46 v. City of Everett
questions: Whether RCW 49.48.030 entitles a labor union to an award of attorney fees for obtaining a favorable wage recovery on behalf of its members in a grievance arbitration.

title: 1515-1519 Lakeview Boulevard Condominium Ass'n v. Apartment Sales Corp.
Department of Ecology v. Campbell & Gwinn, L.L.C.
questions: Whether the statutory exemption from groundwater permit requirements for domestic wells drawing no more than 5,000 gallons per day applies to a subdivision developer proposing multiple wells that will collectively (but not individually) draw more than 5,000 gallons per day.

title: State of Washington v. Moses
questions: Whether the double jeopardy statute, RCW 10.43.040, bars state prosecution after a defendant has been convicted in tribal court for similar offenses based on the same conduct.

title: State of Washington v. Borrero
questions: Whether an information that charges attempted first degree murder but does not expressly allege the "substantial step" element of criminal attempt is constitutionally insufficient and must be dismissed when the document is challenged prior to verdict.

title: City of Spokane v. Marquette
questions: Whether issuance of an arrest warrant for non-compliance with conditions of probation tolls the probationary period and thereby extends a municipal court's jurisdiction to execute on a suspended sentence beyond the two-year statutory limit.

title: State of Washington v. Everybodytalksabout
questions: Whether the prohibition in ER 404(b) on admitting evidence of "other crimes, wrongs, or acts ... to prove the character of a person in order to show action in conformity therewith" applies only to misconduct.

title: City of Spokane v. Department of Revenue
questions: Whether the Department of Revenue erroneously classified the large "interceptor" pipes in Spokane's sewer system as collection lines, rather than transfer lines, for purposes of apportioning income between different excise taxes.

title: Barstad v. Stewart Title Guaranty Co.
questions: Whether a title insurance company can violate the Consumer Protection Act by failing to disclose to a lender that a parcel of land designated to provide security for a loan has never been legally separated from a larger tract.

title: State of Washington v. Cardenas
questions: Whether police officers searching for suspected robbers were justified in entering a motel room, without a warrant or an announcement of their purpose, based on observations made through a gap in the bottom of curtains covering the motel room window.

title: State of Washington v. Koontz
questions: Whether the trial court abused its discretion in allowing the jury, during its deliberations, to review the videotaped testimony of three witnesses.

title: State of Washington v. Rodgers
questions: Whether this prosecution under the drive-by shooting statute, RCW 9A.36.045, against defendants who shot at a home two blocks from where they had left their car, must be dismissed either for insufficient evidence or because the statute is unconstitutionally vague as applied to this conduct.

title: Truck Insurance Exchange v. VanPort Homes, Inc.
questions: Whether a commercial general liability insurer had a duty to defend its insured, a construction consulting firm, when clients sued the firm over its failure to perform contracted services.

title: Firth v. Hefu Lu
questions: Whether an agreement to purchase a cooperative apartment unit falls within the statute of frauds and thus must contain a full legal description of the property. No. 70702-2, Firth (petitioner) v. Lu (respondent).

title: City of Seattle v. Burlington Northern Railroad
questions: Whether Seattle ordinances regulating the switching activities of trains at railroad crossings are preempted by the Interstate Commerce Commission Termination Act or the Federal Railroad Safety Act.

title: Keller v. City of Spokane
questions: Whether a city's duty to design and maintain its streets with ordinary care is owed only to persons who use its streets in a proper manner and exercising due care for their own safety or to all who use its streets.

title: State of Washington v. Jones
questions: Whether the defendant had standing to challenge the search of his girlfriend's purse, left in his car after he (but not the girlfriend) was arrested, and if so, whether the search was invalid.

title: Kamla v. Space Needle Corp.
questions: Whether a landowner is liable under common law and/or statutory law for work-related injuries sustained by an employee of an independent contractor..

title: Rivers v. Washington State Conference of Mason Contractors
questions: Whether the trial court abused its discretion by dismissing a lawsuit for violation of discovery and local scheduling rules.

title: Wingert v. Yellow Freight Systems, Inc.
questions: Whether a collective bargaining agreement can modify the requirements of State regulations regarding employee rest periods and, if not, whether employees have an actionable wage claim for an employer's violation of such regulations.

title: State of Washington v. Coria
questions: Whether community property of a defendant and his spouse can be considered "property of another" for purposes of the malicious mischief statute.

title: State of Washington v. Duncan
questions: Whether police could properly detain the defendant for violation of an "open container" ordinance, having observed him standing at a bus stop shelter near a cold, half-full beer bottle, with the smell of alcohol on his breath.

title: In re Detention of Albrecht
questions: Whether, in a sexually violent predator proceeding involving a person who was released from prison but then reincarcerated for violating a condition of release, the State must prove a recent overt act.

title: Hubbard v. Spokane County
questions: Whether a former county employee may maintain an action for wrongful termination in violation of public policy based on allegations that he was discharged for preventing his supervisor from issuing a zoning permit in violation of the applicable zoning codes.
result: petitioning party received a favorable disposition

title: Mahaney v. Mahaney
questions: Whether the trial court's denial of an Indian mother's motion for return of her children from the custody of a grandparent violated the Indian Child Welfare Act.

title: Samuel's Furniture, Inc. v. Department of Ecology
questions: Whether the Department of Ecology, in enforcing the Shorelines Management Act, must seek review of local government decisions by means of the Land Use Petition Act.

title: Fuentes v. State of Washington
questions: Whether the filing of a personal injury complaint against a public utility district 57 days after a claim was submitted to the district, and 51 days after the district denied the claim, sufficiently complied with the 60-day waiting period requirement of RCW 4.96.020(4).

title: King v. Snohomish County
questions: Whether an offender is entitled to early release credits earned in jail prior to sentencing, when the Department of Corrections later structures the offender's prison sentence to begin with a mandatory deadly weapon enhancement term.

title: Chelan County v. Nykreim
questions: Whether the Land Use Petition Act (LUPA) applies only to quasi-judicial land use decisions and not to ministerial decisions such as a boundary line adjustment by the Chelan County Planning Director.

title: Besel v. Viking Insurance
questions: Whether a settlement between an insured tortfeasor and his injured victim, approved by a trial court as reasonable under the factors enumerated in Chaussee v. Maryland Cas. Co., 60 Wn. App. 504, 803 P.2d 1339, 812 P.2d 487 (1991), binds the insurer in a subsequent suit brought by the victim (as assignee of the insured) alleging insurer bad faith.
result: petitioning party received a favorable disposition

title: Right-Price Recreation, L.L.C. v. Connells Prairie Community Council
questions: Whether the Court of Appeals, having granted discretionary review of an order compelling discovery in this action for slander and commercial disparagement, tortious interference, and civil conspiracy, should also have reviewed a prior order denying a motion to dismiss that was not designated in the notice for discretionary review.

title: State of Washington v. Read
questions: Whether the constitutional standard for harmless error applies to a constitutional evidentiary error made in a criminal bench trial.

title: State of Washington v. Townsend
questions: Whether the Privacy Act, chapter 9.73 RCW, applies to e-mail and real-time computer communications, and if so, whether the defendant in this criminal prosecution impliedly consented to the recording of his communications.

title: Puget Sound Financial, L.L.C. v. Unisearch, Inc.
questions: Whether, in the context of repeated commercial transactions between businesses, limitations on consequential damages printed on regular service invoices are enforceable.

title: State of Washington v. Schultz
questions: Whether a pretrial no-contact order entered pursuant to RCW 10.99.040 remains in effect after the defendant's conviction, based on a provision so specifying in the findings and sentence, but without entry of a post-conviction no-contact order under RCW 10.99.050.

title: Kilian v. Atkinson
questions: A certified question from the United States District Court is whether an age discrimination claim can be asserted by an independent contractor against the City of Chelan and its Mayor under RCW 49.60.030, a provision of the Washington Law Against Discrimination.

title: Olivine Corp. v. United Capitol Insurance
questions: Whether an insurer, when a premium finance company canceled the insurance policy of an incinerator owner for failure to reimburse for the premiums paid, should have notified the owner of the land on which the incinerator was operated.

title: In re Carmick, Attorney at Law
Wagg v. Estate of Dunham
questions: Whether a personal injury lawsuit, seeking liability insurance proceeds against a deceased tortfeasor, requires the filing of a creditor's claim on the estate before the lawsuit can be served.

title: State of Washington v. Westling
questions: The defendant maintains he can be convicted of only one count of second degree arson under RCW 9A.48.030 because he set only one fire. The one fire damaged three automobiles.

title: In re C.W., Petitioner. In the Matter of the Detention of B.B., Petitioner. In the Matter of the Detention of E.S., Petitioner. In the Matter of the Detention of D.M., Petitioner. In the Matter of the Detention of T.B., Petitioner. In the Matter of the Detention of R.F
questions: (1) Whether the six-hour time limit in RCW 71.05.050 begins to run when a person either enters the hospital or is medically cleared or when the professional staff of the hospital determine that the statutory requirements have been met and it is necessary to refer the person to the county designated mental health professional. (2) Whether the latter interpretation of the statute above would violate due process. (3) Whether dismissal is the proper remedy for a violation of RCW 71.05.050.

title: State of Washington v. Barnes
questions: Whether the superior court lost subject matter jurisdiction in a criminal case when the amended information charging the offense of which the defendant was convicted was not filed by the State.

title: In re Personal Restraint of Hutchinson
questions: Whether a criminal defendant claiming diminished capacity was deprived of due process when discovery sanctions were imposed for refusing to submit to a state psychological evaluation after earlier court decisions suggested that he could assert his Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination. See State v. Hutchinson, 111 Wn.2d 872, 766 P.2d 447 (1989).

title: Stansfield v. Douglas County
questions: Whether a plaintiff who moves to amend a complaint under CR 15(c) to add new claims (but not new parties) must show excusable neglect in order to have the amendment relate back to the date of the original complaint.

title: In re King
questions: Whether an offender is entitled to early release credits earned in jail prior to sentencing, when the Department of Corrections later structures the offender's prison sentence to begin with a mandatory deadly weapon enhancement term.

title: WR Enterprises, Inc. v. Department of Labor & Industries
questions: Whether the Department of Labor and Industries' method for setting industrial insurance premiums, which first considers the solvency of the accident and medical aid funds as a whole before setting the rate for each class of employers, is consistent with the Department's statutory authority.

title: In re Mines
questions: Whether a parolee claiming a statutory violation in the conduct of a parole revocation hearing must show prejudice in order to obtain a new hearing.

title: City of Tacoma v. William Rogers Co.
questions: Whether a temporary employment agency may deduct wages paid to temporary workers from its taxable gross income for purposes of Tacoma's Business and Occupation Tax Rule 111.

title: In re Andress
questions: Whether an assault which causes death may constitute the predicate felony for second degree felony murder.

title: Smith v. Whatcom County District Court
questions: Whether a district court has jurisdiction to enforce a misdemeanor fine more than two years after the fine was imposed.

title: In re Goodwin
questions: The petitioner argues that he should be resentenced because prior juvenile convictions that had "washed out" were used in determining his sentence.

title: In re Angeline
questions: Whether a community property agreement terminates as a matter of law when a marriage becomes defunct.

title: The Matter of the Site Certificate Amendment of the Chehalis Generation Facility v. Energy Facility Site Evaluation Council of Washington
questions: Whether these petitioners have properly invoked judicial review of an energy facility siting decision made under chapter 80.50 RCW, and if so, whether the Energy Facility Site Evaluation Council violated the State Environmental Policy Act by failing to perform supplemental environmental analyses for the challenged project.

title: Minton v. Ralston Purina Co.
questions: Whether a worker injured by defective workplace equipment installed by a prior corporate owner of the business may bring a "third person" action under RCW 51.24.030 against his employer, as corporate successor to the prior owner, or against the former corporate parent of the prior owner.

title: In re Detention of Williams
questions: Whether in a sexually violent predator proceeding under chapter 71.09 RCW, the State may move for a mental examination under Civil Rule 35 in addition to the evaluation of a detainee mandated by the statute.

title: In re Mccuistion
questions: Whether in a sexually violent predator proceeding under chapter 71.09 RCW, the State may move for a mental examination under Civil Rule 35 in addition to the evaluation of a detainee mandated by the statute.

title: State of Washington v. Oster
questions: Whether, when the State seeks a felony conviction for willful violation of a court order, the existence of the two similar prior convictions making this crime a felony must be included as an element of the "to convict" instruction, rather than in a separate instruction and verdict form.

title: Boeing Co. v. Heidy
questions: Whether a worker's permanent partial disability award for hearing loss should be reduced to reflect that in addition to occupational causes some hearing loss naturally occurs with age. title: McGowan v. State of Washington
questions: Whether, under Initiative 732 (RCW 28A.400.205), the State must fund cost-of-living pay increases for school district employees whose positions are not funded by the State under its constitutional obligation to provide basic education.

title: State of Washington v. Moreno
questions: Whether the trial court, in a traffic infraction proceeding not attended by a prosecuting attorney, violated the defendant's due process rights by calling to testify and questioning the citing officer and the radar expert.

title: Blume v. Department of Social & Health Services
questions: Whether, in this child dependency action under chapter 13.34 RCW, relatives of the children who had filed an independent custody petition under chapter 26.10 RCW could properly intervene and object to a dependency order agreed to by the parents and DSHS.

title: Bell v. State of Washington
questions: Whether, in this action claiming negligent supervision of a parolee, the trial court erred in refusing to instruct the jury on the burden of proof at a parole revocation hearing, or by refusing to strike testimony about that standard by a former member of the Indeterminate Sentence Review Board.

title: Regional Disposal Co. v. City of Centralia
questions: Whether the City of Centralia's tax on the business of transferring solid waste from trucks to railroad cars is preempted by federal railroad law, is unconstitutionally vague, conflicts with state solid waste management statutes, or unlawfully imposes a tax on counties or on revenues derived from activities conducted outside city limits.

title: State of Washington v. Linehan
questions: Whether, in this first degree theft prosecution, the jury was correctly instructed on the definition of theft by means of "exerting unauthorized control" and, if not, whether the error was harmless.

title: Williamson, Inc. v. Calibre Homes, Inc.
questions: Whether the substantial compliance doctrine applies to the Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons Act.

title: State of Washington v. Lopez
questions: Whether upon remand for resentencing the State may present evidence of prior convictions in support of a persistent offender sentence, following reversal of such a sentence because the trial court ruled such evidence unnecessary.

title: State of Washington v. Watson
questions: Whether under RCW 13.40.127, which prohibits a juvenile court from deferring a disposition if the juvenile "has a prior deferred disposition or deferred adjudication," a juvenile court may defer disposition of separately charged offenses considered in a single disposition hearing.

title: State of Washington v. Martin
questions: Whether a driver has a reasonable expectation of privacy in Department of Licensing records that precludes police from constitutionally searching those records by computer without an individualized suspicion that the driver is involved in criminal activity.

title: City of Everett, Respondent, v. Randal D. Schroeder, Petitioner
questions: Whether a driver has a reasonable expectation of privacy in Department of Licensing records that precludes police from constitutionally searching those records by computer without an individualized suspicion that the driver is involved in criminal activity.

title: State of Washington v. McKinney
questions: Whether a driver has a reasonable expectation of privacy in Department of Licensing records that precludes police from constitutionally searching those records by computer without an individualized suspicion that the driver is involved in criminal activity.

title: State of Washington v. Glossbrener
questions: Whether police, who stopped the defendant's car on a routine traffic matter, permissibly searched the unoccupied car based on officer safety concerns where the officer allowed the defendant to remain in his car for a period of time and then had him get out the car to perform sobriety tests before conducting the search.

title: In re Wright
questions: When valuing a vested but unmatured pension at dissolution by reducing it to present value, must the trial court, as a matter of law, base its calculations on the earliest date at which the pension matures, or may the court in its discretion use the later date of the employee-spouse's likely retirement?

title: Stelter v. State of Washington
questions: Whether this industrial insurance claim against an interstate trucking company was properly dismissed based on the common carrier exemption from mandatory industrial insurance coverage (RCW 51.12.095(1)), where the claimant truck driver, injured during an interstate trip, averred that he did not know of or consent to his employment by this company for interstate trips and a separate company for intrastate trips.

title: In re Fawcett
questions: Whether a defendant's guilty plea is voluntary when the defendant is told he will serve at least one year of community placement when the applicable mandatory term is at least two years.

title: State of Washington v. Kilgore
questions: Whether a trial court must hold an evidentiary hearing before admitting contested evidence of prior uncharged acts under ER 404(b).

title: In re Hemenway
questions: Whether a defendant's plea of "guilty" is facially invalid because he was not informed at the time he entered his plea that mandatory community placement was a direct consequence.

title: All Around Underground v. State of Washington
questions: Whether impoundment of a vehicle pursuant to a State Patrol rule (WAC 204-96-010) that mandates impoundment when the driver has a suspended license, without considering reasonable alternatives to impoundment, violates either the Fourth Amendment or Const. art. 1, § 7.

title: State of Washington v. Crawford
questions: Whether a defendant, by invoking the marital privilege and thus making his wife an unavailable witness, thereby waives his confrontation clause objection to admission of his wife's prior statement to police.
result: petitioning party received a favorable disposition

title: State of Washington v. A.M.R.
questions: Whether the Court of Appeals properly allowed the State to appeal juvenile restitution orders under RAP 2.2(b), and if so, whether the juvenile court erred in declining to award restitution to the insurers of primary victims.

title: Thurston County v. Cooper Point Ass'n
questions: Whether an extension of a sewer line through a rural area to reach and serve existing residential communities is "necessary to protect basic public health and safety and the environment," and thus exempt from the development prohibition of RCW 36.70A.110(4).

title: City of Seattle v. Allison
questions: Whether the results of a DUI defendant's breath test were properly suppressed on the ground that the prosecution could not show that the simulator solution temperature met the requirements specified by former WAC 448-13-040 in order to establish a foundation for admission of the results.

title: State of Washington v. Cannon
questions: Whether Washington Administrative Code (WAC) 448-13-040 requires the proponent of the breath test in an implied consent proceeding to produce evidence that the thermometer used in the test was certified as required by WAC 448-13-035.

title: Willoughby v. State of Washington
questions: Whether the cancellation of permanent partial disability benefits to incarcerated workers under RCW 51.32.040(3)(a), as applied to Respondents under RCW 72.60.102, violates equal protection or due process, when Respondents are unlikely to be released during their lifetimes and do not have a statutory beneficiary to whom the benefits may be transferred, and whether this provision is consistent with RCW 9.92.110 (barring forfeiture of a prisoner's property by reason of his or her conviction).

title: City of Seattle v. Patu
questions: Whether a defendant convicted of obstructing a public officer, in violation of Seattle Municipal Code 12A.16.010(A)(5), may challenge on appeal a "to convict" instruction he proposed, on the basis that the instruction omitted the element of actual obstruction.

title: Hauber v. Yakima County
questions: Whether the estate of a fire fighter who died during a Yakima County Search and Rescue dive in an irrigation siphon, after being called away from duty at the Yakima city fire station, may maintain a wrongful death action against the county. See RCW 38.52.080(1); RCW 38.52.190.

title: State of Washington v. Clausing
questions: Whether RCW 69.41.030, which makes it a crime to deliver a legend drug except upon the order or prescription of a physician, prohibits an unlicensed practitioner from filling a valid prescription.

title: State of Washington v. Smith
questions: Whether the trial court, before finding a child victim unavailable to testify for purposes of the admission of hearsay under RCW 9A.44.120, should determine whether the child can testify by closed-circuit television as provided in RCW 9A.44.150.

title: State of Washington v. Sorrells
questions: Whether the voyeurism statute, RCW 9A.44.115, criminalizes photographing or videotaping up a women's skirt in a public place, and if so, whether the statute is unconstitutionally vague or overbroad.

title: Fraternal Order of Eagles, Tenino Aerie No. 564 v. Grand Aerie of Fraternal Order of Eagles
questions: Whether a fraternal organization must prove it is "distinctly private" in nature in order to qualify for exemption under the Washington Law Against Discrimination, RCW 49.60.040(10).

title: State of Washington v. Glas
questions: Whether the voyeurism statute, RCW 9A.44.115, criminalizes photographing or videotaping up a women's skirt in a public place, and if so, whether the statute is unconstitutionally vague or overbroad.

title: In re Kuvara, Attorney at Law
Washington State Labor Council v. Reed
State of Washington v. Vasquez
questions: Whether a determination in an administrative license suspension hearing that police lacked probable cause to stop a driver precludes a trial court from revisiting that issue in a subsequent criminal prosecution.

title: One Pacific Towers Homeowners' Ass'n v. HAL Real Estate Investments, Inc.
questions: Whether a real estate investment corporation and/or its subsidiaries were "declarants" or "dealers" under the state condominium act and were therefore required to provide public offering statements when they sold their condominium units.

title: State of Washington v. Beaver
questions: Whether the juvenile court or the Department of Social and Health Services sets the minimum term of confinement for a juvenile offender when the court determines that a standard range sentence would constitute a manifest injustice.

title: State of Washington v. Vickers
questions: Whether the affidavit based upon information provided by a confidential informant was sufficient for issuance of a search warrant; whether a photomontage used to identify an offender was impermissibly suggestive; and whether a prior out-of-state conviction was sufficiently proven under the Persistent Offender Act.
